Projects.Name: Pixel Pundits
Projects.Description: This is my Senior Project at the University of Florida. It is a web app that serves as a trading platform for players of the Magic: The Gathering trading card game. The app works like a digital marketplace where users can upload their collection, search for cards they want, and offer to trade cards with other users. I was involved with most of the front-end development, designing many of the page layouts and the overall UI. I also designed the API calls to the Scryfall API, which provided card data including images and pricing.

Projects.Name: Contagion Simulator
Projects.Description: Inspired by the COVID pandemic, I wanted to create a way to simulate virus transmission within a population. The program takes in a variety of user-set factors, such as population size, lethality, and immunity, then runs randomly generated cycles to see the various outcomes of those inputs. For example, a user who wanted to see the effect of natural immunity on the spread of a virus could set the built-up immunity value very high. The UI is built with the Pygame library.

Projects.Name: Calculator
Projects.Description: This project was influenced by the semester-long project of the University of Florida's Programming Language Concepts course, where the goal was to take a fictional programming language and convert it into executable Java code. That was done through a series of steps: breaking the text down into tokens with regex, grouping the tokens into abstract syntax trees, type checking the values, and finally translating the result. The Calculator is built on that premise: the user provides a mathematical expression that is run through a similar series of steps, except a calculation is made instead of translating to Java code. The UI was built with JFrame and testing was done with JUnit.
